Open Question: Why such little love for Gentoo?

I was into Gentoo like 10 years ago. Then I realized that the Ubuntu crowd was getting kernels as fast as I was for a tenth the effort.

Building from scratch just forget seem with the effort anymore, I've got work to get done.

Gentoo is always, just one, difficult to find, typo away from trashing the whole system. Worst, rebuilding the system is no quick feat.
Today, glibc-2.25-r8 has just been marked at stable with a new version.... and I wait to find if something I've done will cause it to break anything. Having the core library, which everything else is built on, update on the fly is a impressive feat that works most of the time. That's what Gentoo really is, an impressive game of rolling dice. I've lost only a few times.
Less people use Gentoo since it almost always requires a second computer at some point. I have the desktop and a laptop I send tested bin-packages to, so at least one machine is still working. I am my own final quality check.
Because compiling everything is a PITA and doesn't bring much improvements.

I use Gentoo on all my AMD machines, because AMD usually doesn't get compiler optimizations that Intel does, and compiling on your own makes a bigger difference (from my experience) with AMD than it does Intel.

Gentoo is an extremely good distro to learn Linux with. You will break your system and you will cause a lot of problems, but everything you need to know to fix it is there, without having to wipe and reinstall. I think after using Gentoo for years and years, the allure is fading, and it's not as cool as it used to be.

But I still stick with it, because it's really the only major distro where you basically just get a package manager and then build up the rest of the system how you want. I don't know where else to get a systemd, pulse audio free system with whatever DE you want. There's even GNOME3 without systemd on Gentoo (and Funtoo, which is a fork of Gentoo that has some changes to the package manager).

Gentoo project is really amazing, it does deserve a lot more love. But I think people get turned off by it because it will take a lot of botched updates and mistakes before you get a system where you stop breaking it. I admittedly used to break my Gentoo quite often back in the day, but now I have learned and now I don't make nearly the mistakes I used to.

I've lost a lot of will to promote Gentoo though and talk about how great it is. Mainly because there's so many idiots out there who act like "more coars" is such a horrible thing, and then turn around and say Gentoo is a waste of time because it takes forever to compile. At risk of sounding like an AMD fanboy , AMD has been offering very good multi-thread performance at a very good price for a long time, even FX 8350 was a very good value in situations like running Gentoo. I have a Ryzen 1700x right now, and compiling everything for a deep system update only takes a few hours, as long as I don't wait too long between updates.

Just looking at newegg randomly, I see 8 core Ryzen 1700 for $299 on sale. I don't think in this age there's much validity to complaining about compile times. If you are and you have a new desktop computer, you're doing something very wrong.
